results.title: The route model
results.summary: Rewrote `LEGS` to the six-leg route (`bay, ideate, specify, execute, review, cleanup`), added `OFF_ROUTE_BOOKINGS`/`BOOKABLE_IDS`, deleted `ideateIsDone` and the index-0 branch in the inference walk, and ran the three-way booking and fixture rename (`ideation-ideate`→`ideation-brainstorm`, `ideation-contract`→`ideation-ideate` absorbing `ideation-refine`, `openspec-specs`→`openspec-specify`; same order in `tests/fixtures/`). Inner loop `node --test tests/legs.test.js tests/bookings.test.js tests/inference.test.js` is 122/122 green and all five phase-1 success-criteria greps pass; the phase gate `node --test tests/` is 580 pass / 38 fail, and every remaining failure is in the expected-red set the spec declares (goldens and leg-name literals in tests/waybill.test.js, the help-card route table, tests/guide.test.js — all phase 4; plus three `waybill new` cases in tests/cli.test.js that phase 2's `firstLeg` rework owns). Three gaps the spec under-specified were resolved: six extra `knownLegs` call sites beyond the four named (tests/bookings.test.js, bookings-overlay, booking-swap, inspection-gitignore, review, commands) all moved to `BOOKABLE_IDS`; the fixture count is `LEGS.length + 2` (brainstorm joins no-docket as a non-leg fixture) since the spec's "exactly seven files" is arithmetically impossible; and the `LegFixture` typedef, stranded by `ideate.js` changing meaning, moved to `tests/helpers/repo-fixture.js`. Also kept `parseTarget` on route ids rather than `BOOKABLE_IDS`, so `<branch>/brainstorm` stays a branch name rather than becoming a leg token. — Every cycle-1 finding is resolved: both blocking findings (the `waybill new` carrier assertions at tests/cli.test.js:493,535 and the stale `names the stamp for each shipped leg` map at tests/help.test.js:151-161) are fixed and documented, the three mediums are fixed, and all five lows are addressed either in code or in the spec's new Implementation Notes and Open Items. I re-traced the changed skip/complete arithmetic at tests/inference.test.js:253-270 and the positional leg strip at tests/waybill.test.js:586-596 by hand and both are correct, checked for orphaned imports and constants after the `BOOKABLE_IDS` fan-out and found none, and confirmed no retired leg id reaches a validated `knownLegs` set — the only surviving `refine`/`contract`/`specs` literals are the deliberate retired-id rejection case at tests/bookings.test.js:385 and self-contained synthetic maps. The four remaining findings are all comment accuracy and spec bookkeeping; nothing blocks the commit.

results.title: The new on-ramp
results.summary: Reworked `/waybill:new` into an off-route on-ramp: `firstLeg` (renamed `onRamp`) now builds the brainstorm state unconditionally via `OFF_ROUTE_BOOKINGS[0]` instead of `LEGS[0]`, drops `index`, rewords the docket-open warning, and `begin` appends a new `AFTER THE BRAINSTORM:` section carrying `/waybill:bay <branch>` after the rendered block; `commands/new.md` records the deliberate inversion of `commands/bay.md`'s "do not invent a branch" rule and scopes "only the last" to the NEXT: block; captured `tests/golden/new.txt`. NOTE: I deliberately did NOT create `tests/golden/new.md` (the spec's other New File) — `new --markdown` exits 2 and is pinned so by two tests, so no code path can produce it; the scout's risk 2 sanctions this and the contract criterion greps only `new.txt`. Also left for phase 5, per the scout's risk 5: the now-false one-liners at `src/cli.js:38` (USAGE) and `src/help.js:30,52`. Unrelated observation: `tests/booking-swap.test.js` gained uncommitted edits during my run that I did not make (a concurrent sibling stage, most likely) — it is excluded from filesChanged. — Phase 2 is implemented cleanly and largely exceeds the spec: `onRamp` resolves the brainstorm through `OFF_ROUTE_BOOKINGS[0]` rather than `LEGS[0]`, drops `index`, rewords the warning without naming a leg, and appends an `AFTER THE BRAINSTORM:` section outside the `NEXT:` block so "run only the last line" cannot reach it — with `tests/golden/new.txt` matching `bookings/ideation-brainstorm.md` byte for byte, and tests covering every case the spec's Testing Requirements list (booking command/model/effort, no `leg N of M`, the `<branch>` fallback, the reworded in-bay warning, the outside-a-repo exit 2). `src/waybill.js` is untouched as the decision log demands, and the two spec snippets the builder deviated from (the `!docketOpen` early return, and deriving the branch name in the CLI) are both deviations in the correct direction. No critical or high findings: the remaining issues are a missing `new.md` golden the spec asked for, two phase-3 test files sitting in the same working tree, and one stale fixture comment — none of which block the commit, though the commit should be scoped to phase 2's own files.
findings: medium/spec-deviation tests/golden/new.md:missing — The spec's New Files table requires both `tests/golden/new.txt` and `tests/golden/new.md`; only `new.txt` was created. The omission is defensible (`begin` at /Users/jtinetti/Projects/tinetti/waybill/.claude/worktrees/waybill-feat-leg-renames/src/cli.js:501-505 rejects every argument, so `new --markdown` exits 2, and tests/commands.test.js already pins that new.md never mentions `--markdown`), but the deviation is only recorded in the builder's own context-map gate table → Either add the renderer-level markdown golden the way tests/waybill.test.js:148 produces `no-docket.md`, or state in the phase-2 commit message (and ideally in spec-phase-2.md's File Changes) that `new.md` is deliberately not created because `new` has no markdown surface, so phase 4's golden sweep does not go looking for it.

medium/spec-deviation tests/doctor.test.js:416-443, tests/booking-swap.test.js:66-79,156-176 — These two additions are phase 3's deliverables verbatim (spec-phase-3.md:52-53: the retired-leg overlay doctor warn case and the brainstorm-carrier overlay rebooking case); spec-phase-2.md's Modified Files table lists only src/cli.js, commands/new.md, tests/cli.test.js and tests/commands.test.js. If they land inside the phase-2 commit, phase 3 has nothing left to commit and the run's 5/5 commit accounting breaks → Scope the phase-2 commit to the spec's File Changes (plus the phase-1 leftovers the context map names) and leave tests/doctor.test.js and tests/booking-swap.test.js unstaged for phase 3's commit; do not revert them, since contract-data.json:201 runs phases 2 and 3 as a parallel wave and they may be the other phase's in-flight work.

medium/testing tests/fixtures/no-docket.js:7-11 — The fixture's doc comment still claims "`no-docket.txt` is leg 1's waybill, and since the exit contract landed it is what `waybill new` prints" and that the golden is "asserted twice … through the verb in `tests/cli.test.js`". This change made both claims false: cli.test.js:486 now asserts `new`, and no CLI verb prints `no-docket.txt`. The comment is the exact kind of stale pairing the spec's Failure Modes table calls out, and a later reader could delete `new.txt`'s coverage on its authority → Rewrite it the way tests/waybill.test.js:174-179's comment was rewritten in this same diff: no-docket.* is the renderer's own no-docket contract, claimed by no verb.

low/spec-deviation src/cli.js:435 — `firstLeg` was renamed to `onRamp` and the `if (!state.docketOpen) return state;` early return from the spec's code snippet was dropped in favour of building unconditionally. Both deviations are correct — after phase 1 the pass-through would hand off `bay`, and `docketOpen` is false only on the trunk or a detached HEAD (src/inference.js:107), where `defaultBranch(root)` is the honest branch — but the spec's snippet says otherwise → Record the two corrections in the commit message so the next reader does not treat the snippet as the authority.

low/spec-deviation src/cli.js:466-481 — The Full-tier branch proposal is implemented in commands/new.md rather than in `bayHandoff`, which always renders the `<branch>` placeholder. This is the only layer that can see a brainstorm conclusion, and the spec's own fallback requirement is met, but the spec's Technical Approach reads as if the CLI derives the name → Note in the commit message that the derivation lives in the session instructions and the CLI holds the fallback, so the tier is not later read as unimplemented.

results.title: Evidence for the out-of-scope claims
results.summary: Added the two missing test cases that back the contract's out-of-scope claims: a `tests/doctor.test.js` case proving a retired leg id (`leg: specs`) in a bookings overlay degrades to WARN with `unknown leg `specs`` and the offending file path while doctor still exits 0 and renders every other row, and a `tests/booking-swap.test.js` case proving the brainstorm carrier is rebookable through the overlay tier (`resolveBookings` + `WAYBILL_BOOKINGS_DIR`) rather than only by editing the shipped file — the overlay-layered variant, chosen over a near-duplicate of the in-place swap that already landed in 456f7d8. Both were verified non-tautological by temporarily flipping the fixture (valid leg id → `info (1 legs rebooked)`; no overlay → assertion fails). Inner loop 41/41 green; phase gate is 620 tests / 588 pass / 32 fail, the same 32 golden/guide/help/cli/fleet failures owned by phases 2 and 4 (pass count rose 586→588, fail count unchanged). Note: `src/cli.js`, `tests/cli.test.js` and `tests/commands.test.js` acquired modifications in this worktree partway through the run — they are not mine (a concurrent sibling or prior run) and are excluded from filesChanged, as are the pre-existing `tests/frontmatter.test.js` / `tests/help.test.js` edits. — The two test cases the phase-3 spec actually asks for are well built and non-tautological: the doctor case (tests/doctor.test.js:417-444) copies the :401-411 duplicate-leg pattern, swaps in a genuinely retired `specs` id with a stampPath so the leg gate is what throws, and asserts WARN positively plus the file path, exit 0 and the surviving rows; the rebooking case (tests/booking-swap.test.js:155-175) asserts the resolved command with and without the overlay through a helper that mirrors bookings-overlay.test.js's isolated() wrapper exactly. Neither has a critical or high defect, so phase 3's own work is ready. The blockers are around it rather than in it: the tree also holds an uncommitted phase-2 build with no phase-2 commit behind it, tests/golden/new.txt is untracked rather than `git add -N`'d, and commands/new.md changed mid-review — commit phase 2 separately and stage only the two test files for phase 3, or the 5/5 commit count is unreachable.

results.title: Goldens, the ride-along, and the test sweep
results.summary: Turned the suite green: deleted the six orphaned goldens (contract.*, refine.*, specs.* — the latter re-minted as specify.*), re-blessed all 22 remaining goldens from real CLI output via the existing UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 mechanism (the spec wrongly claimed none exists), rewrote docs/guide/01-ride-along.md's headings and ```waybill fences for the six-leg route (brainstorm section unnumbered and its fence dropped; refine+contract merged into Leg 2 · ideate), and corrected six stale leg-name/route-length comments in src/fleet.js, src/progress.js and src/waybill.js. Validation: `node --test tests/guide.test.js tests/cli.test.js` 98/98 pass; `node --test tests/` 624/624 pass, exit 0 (baseline was 31 failing). Two caveats for the commit stage: (a) tests/frontmatter.test.js and tests/help.test.js carry pre-existing uncommitted edits from earlier phases and are included in filesChanged deliberately — without them the committed tree is red; (b) per scout risk 5, src/help.js:30,52 ("leg 1's waybill", surfaced at tests/golden/help.txt:4,31) is still factually wrong after the rework and is unclaimed by any phase — left for phase 5 as it is outside this spec's file list. — All three actionable cycle-1 findings are fixed: the bay waybill now compares itself to the cleanup leg across bookings/waybill-bay.md:14 and all four re-blessed goldens plus the ride-along fence; the help card's `new` row was reworded in src/help.js:30,52 and src/cli.js:38 with help.txt re-blessed and tests/help.test.js:259-264 updated to justify the one deliberate change to its frozen usage copy; and the five retired `specs` fixture keys in tests/inspection-gitignore.test.js are now `specify`. I independently verified the phase's load-bearing coupling read-only: all six ` ```waybill ` fences in docs/guide/01-ride-along.md match their leg golden byte for byte, headings are numbered 1-6 in LEGS order, ideate.{txt,md} is a real content swap rather than a rename, contract criterion 37's positive and negative greps both hold, and no golden or src/ file retains a retired leg id. Only low findings remain, every one of them prose that spec-phase-5.md:56 explicitly claims, so this is ready to commit; note that I did not execute the suite, since the reviewer role restricts Bash to read-only inspection.

results.title: Prose surfaces
results.summary: SCOUT UNAVAILABLE for "Prose surfaces" (agent stalled on all 6 attempts (no progress for 180000ms each)) — the builder explored inline and no context map was written. — Swept every prose surface outside guide.test.js's mechanical coupling onto the six-leg route: the root README (route table, samples, leg numbers, prerequisites, `waybill new` prose), all four docs/guide files, the three `fix/specs` collision sites re-pointed to `fix/specify`, the live add-help-card change's design route table and pinned stamp scenario, and the command-surface spec's retired-leg scenarios. Added CHANGELOG.md with an Unreleased BREAKING note on machine-local overlays binding a retired leg id, naming `waybill doctor` as the recovery path and no version number. — All six cycle-1 findings are fixed: the living `new` requirement and its scenarios in openspec/specs/command-surface/spec.md are rewritten around the off-route brainstorm and its `/waybill:bay` handoff (matching commands/new.md and tests/golden/new.txt), add-help-card's proposal.md and tasks.md now say six-leg/six phrases, the CHANGELOG gained the `ideate`-changed-meaning paragraph and the doctor exception, reference.md's booking fence lead-in was softened, and the ride-along now quotes the `AFTER THE BRAINSTORM:` lines verbatim as an indented block (no ```waybill fence, so guide.test.js:145 stays green). The phase's inner-loop grep over README.md, docs/guide/, openspec/specs/command-surface/spec.md and openspec/changes/add-help-card/ exits 1 (no matches), and the route table, fleet sample, help-card ROUTE block and stamp phrases all match src/legs.js, tests/golden/help.txt and the shipped bookings row for row. Two non-blocking medium findings remain — an overstated \"only doctor survives\" claim repeated in CHANGELOG.md and 03-reference.md, and one stale `Legs 5 and 6` JSDoc in src/doctor.js — so this is commit-ready; I did not run `node --test tests/` (read-only review), though the only source/test edits move in matched pairs.
findings: medium/logic CHANGELOG.md:18 — The note's survivor claim is too narrow in both places it is made: `:18` says the failure hits "every `/waybill:*` command, and every `waybill` verb but `doctor`", and `:27` says "**`waybill doctor` is the one command that still runs.**" `help` also survives by design — `src/help.js:121-126` catches the `resolveBookings` throw, renders em-dash rows plus one line naming the problem and exits 0, which is the `add-help-card` requirement "The page never fails over its bookings" (openspec/changes/add-help-card/specs/help-card/spec.md:86-94). Both `commands/help.md` and `commands/doctor.md` exist, so `/waybill:help` and `/waybill:doctor` survive too and the `/waybill:*` half of the sentence is also wrong. Telling a stranded operator that the page they reach for when lost is dead is the opposite of the note's stated discovery job → Name `help` alongside `doctor` in both sentences (e.g. "every `/waybill:*` command and every `waybill` verb except `doctor` and `help`"), and apply the same correction to the identical claim at docs/guide/03-reference.md:139-142 ("`waybill doctor` is the one command that keeps running").
